summary: The exact candidate provides a functional opt-in atomic warmup marker and passes its regression suite, but its compatibility key does not exactly identify the DeepGEMM/JIT implementation. An independent adversarial test changed a JIT source file outside deep_gemm.__file__ without changing the candidate identity, permitting an incompatible restored cache to skip warmup.

tests.what_was_measured: Original behavior reproduced directly: two process-equivalent calls retaining the same cache both dispatched the all-M warmup (warmup_calls=2).
Candidate regression suite: nine marker serialization, invalidation, dispatch, partial-coverage, and failure-path tests passed.

Positive independent restored-cache case passed (one warmup, one marker), then the exact-identity adversarial assertion failed: changing a sibling DeepGEMM JIT source file left _module_identity unchanged.
No whitespace errors in the candidate diff.

gpu_execution_evidence: The only assigned device was an AMD Instinct MI350X under ROCm 7.2. The prepared environment had no CUDA runtime and no deep_gemm package; no unrelated ROCm execution was counted as DeepGEMM validation.
remaining_counterexamples: A DeepGEMM installation can change JIT generator or native implementation files outside deep_gemm.__file__ while retaining the same package version and __init__.py. The candidate then computes the same compatibility identity and may skip warmup for an incompatible restored cache.
remaining_limitations: Real NVIDIA DeepGEMM JIT compilation and restored-cache reuse were unavailable.
Independent GPU numerical comparison and CUDA graph parity were unavailable.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro TP=8 startup latency and steady-state inference performance were unavailable.
No native source changed in the candidate, so native rebuild was not applicable.
